exercise.name: Dumbbell Lateral Walk

reference.title: Dumbbell Lateral Walk (male)
reference.listing: Video; the page could not be read here (blocked), so the movement follows the name and standard coaching (half squat, dumbbells at the sides, side steps).

exercise.mechanics: Compound (side steps in a half squat)

breathing.pattern: Breathe steadily, one breath per step; keep the trunk braced.

prescription.tempo: Controlled; stay at the same height
prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbells; posture and depth first
prescription.progression: Lower squat, longer distance, then heavier dumbbells

cues.text: Dumbbells at your sides, feet hip width; sit into a half squat, chest up.
Step the right foot out to the side; stay low, toes forward.
Bring the left foot in after it to hip width; do not stand up between steps.
Hold the half squat; weight in the middle of the feet.
Now lead with the left foot out to the left.
Bring the right foot in after it, back to the start.

mistakes.mistake: Bobbing up and down with each step
mistakes.fix: Keep the hips at the same height; the knees stay bent.
The trailing foot stops at hip width.
Push the knees out over the toes.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding forward or shrugging under the dumbbells
mistakes.fix: Chest up, shoulders down, arms long.

kinematics.norm: Half squat held through the steps (about 40-50 degrees of knee bend; clinical opinion)
Side steps of about a foot length, trailing foot back to hip width (clinical opinion)
Hips back with a slight forward lean, back flat (clinical opinion)
Long, dumbbells at the sides (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s per step (clinical opinion); gluteus medius is a key frontal-plane hip stabiliser in abduction tasks (Macadam 2015)

sources.title: GymVisual #17978, Dumbbell Lateral Walk (male), video (movement reference)
Macadam, Cronin & Contreras 2015, gluteal muscle activity in dynamic hip abduction and hip external rotation exercise: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 10(5):573-591; PMC4595911)
Winwood, Cronin, Brown & Keogh 2014, a biomechanical analysis of the farmers walk, and comparison with the deadlift and unloaded walk (Int J Sports Sci Coach 9(5):1127-1143)

cautions: Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Knee pain: squat higher and take shorter steps.
Clear a straight lane to the side; look where you step.
Set the dumbbells down with a flat back if the grip fades.
Load is user-chosen: start with light dumbbells.

muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Abducts the stepping leg and holds the pelvis level over the stance leg; a key target of frontal-plane hip exercises (Macadam 2015).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Abducts the stepping leg and holds the pelvis level over the stance leg; a key target of frontal-plane hip exercises (Macadam 2015).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Holds the half squat and helps push the body sideways (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Holds the half squat and helps push the body sideways (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Hold the knees bent through every step (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Hold the knees bent through every step (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Bring the trailing leg in and control the wide stance (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Bring the trailing leg in and control the wide stance (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Support the hip hinge of the half squat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Support the hip hinge of the half squat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Push off and steady the ankles (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Push off and steady the ankles (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still as the weight shifts from foot to foot (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the back flat in the half squat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the back flat in the half squat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the dumbbells (Winwood 2014 described grip as a limiter in loaded carries).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the dumbbells (Winwood 2014 described grip as a limiter in loaded carries).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the shoulders under the dumbbells (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Hold the shoulders under the dumbbells (clinical opinion).
